design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0, frozen 2026-11-09 10:40:00 EST (rework round 9).
DRAW: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,4,4] -> estimate_month_trueup 5, actual_month_cost_cap 4, eligible_advance_payment 4.
WHY A GOOD TEST: a POA son of a newly approved dual-eligible resident, now on hospice, asks for one ACH amount that brings patient pay current and covers December. The figure exists only after the agent sees that (1) October, the last closed month billed on the notice, still carries its full 2245.90 charge although the Medical Assistance program bore cost only for 7 Medicaid days, all after the 2026-10-25 hospice election and so priced at the 95% room-and-board share - the 21 Part A coinsurance days carry nothing because their coinsurance is billed to the resident and the Plan L carrier, the 10-08/09 hospital leave sat on a Medicare-stay hold the resident pays, and on 10-24 the resident was paying under her option-1 advance notice; and (2) September, the latest estimate month, reconciles to an actual patient pay of 0.00 (skilled admission 2026-09-03, 19 full-coverage days, a lapsed-certification day, 5 coinsurance days at nothing, a privately held hospital day, a declined leave and a day after a released hold). Only then is the balance right (1910.94 owed: the November charge, whose standing trust transfer falls due on 11-10, net of the October credit), and the advance is the December notice amount (2229.70 from 2026-12-01) less the payee funds (the 1783.50 benefit rather than the later 64.20 deposit, plus the 216.00 pension under the standing authorization, less the 45.00 personal needs allowance kept in the account) plus that balance.
REALISM: the cost of care counts what the Medical Assistance program bears: Medicaid days at the daily rate (hospice days at the tier's 95% room-and-board share, 42 USC 1396a(a)(13)(B)); a coinsurance day only where the program is billed it as crossover payer, never above its daily rate; nothing for Part A full-coverage days, lapsed-certification days (medicare base: provider liable), privately held days (paid on the bed-hold record), days the resident pays under an option-1 or option-2 SNF ABN or that a timely review holds (medicare base), or days away with no bed held. Nothing is collected twice.
SCOPE: task 0 claims medicaid_ext_actual_month_cost_cap, medicaid_ext_estimate_month_trueup, medicaid_ext_eligible_advance_payment (tools post_cost_of_care_reduction_89ef8a19, post_trueup_decrease_6ec57e06, pay_patient_pay_advance_e93eb0b7); task 1 holds the pending-case pair.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root eligible_advance_payment (user). Edge A (value_input, state form): 'The advance is fixed only after the actual charge of the last closed month stands at no more than that month's cost of care.' - false at opening (October charge 2245.90, no cost_of_care_cap reduction, October cost 1910.94); only post_cost_of_care_reduction_89ef8a19 posts that reduction. Edge B (value_input, state form): 'The advance is not fixed until the latest month billed as an estimate stands reconciled to the actual patient pay of that month.' - false at opening (September estimate 2245.90, no trueup_decrease, actual 0.00); only post_trueup_decrease_6ec57e06 posts it. A and B commute. Deletion: skip A -> advance 2521.10; skip B -> 4432.04; gold 2186.14. Persona names no prerequisite; tools check nothing but a positive amount.
OVERRIDES: the cost-of-care clause is retired by the three reviews with ONE shared scope sentence; the partial-month clause by the reconciliation and the pending-month review with one shared sentence restating it verbatim (the actual-month review does not retire it, covers only a resident with exactly one funds account, exactly one Medicare coverage episode and no bed hold ended by a discharge elsewhere - Lorraine qualifies - and posts nothing for any other resident or for a month carrying the partial-month rule's entries or a discharge/death record); the reconciliation retires the trueup-decrease clause for the latest estimate month; the refund clause only for a fresh credit when a representative pays toward the coming month. Out of scope every policy computes the base rule exactly (actual months: (calendar days - booked held days - days away with no bed held) x rate; estimate months: the accrual's days in the center x rate).
FACTOR CARD (T1 own world; T2 on scratch worlds in worklog round 4): cost cap 334.96 - actual_coinsurance_day_price (parameter; no crossover -> 0; T1 0.00), actual_hospice_share_start (parameter; election inside October -> 10-25; T1 234.38), actual_days_after_coverage (method; option-1 notice -> 1 day; T1 47.60), actual_privately_held_start (parameter; Medicare-stay hold -> leave start; T1 0.00); all-baseline 0.00. Reconciliation 2245.90 - reconciled_coinsurance_day_price (1160.90), reconciled_privately_held_start (1958.54), reconciled_declined_hold_days (1958.54), reconciled_released_hold_days (1958.54), reconciled_days_outside_stay (1671.18); all-baseline 0.00. Advance 2186.14 - approved_payee_benefit_applied (3905.44), approved_authorized_pension (2402.14), approved_amount_kept (2141.14), approved_balance_carried (275.20); all-baseline 2165.50.
NEAR-MISSES: the 2026-11 actual charge (current month); the 64.20 deposit (latest by date, not the larger figure); the October booking of 21 days; the September declined and released reservations (read only by the reconciliation); the unpaid November charge (its standing transfer falls due 11-10); the trust resource-limit notices (not deposits); the current notice (2229.70, effective December) versus the October charge (2245.90) that sets September's notice patient pay; the open October Plan L resident coinsurance (a Medicare-record balance, not patient pay).
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: adjustments - medicaid_evt_patient_pay_actual.adjust_once (no reduction of either reason on either charge); payment - medicaid_evt_payments / medicaid_agg_case_balances (ACH accepted). No time gate; the reconciliation service standard (30 days from the 2026-10-02 approval) has passed, which leaves it owed.
SEED: admitted 2026-09-03 from UPMC Harrisburg after a 6-midnight stay; Part A Plan L (not QMB) through 2026-10-23 (NOMNC 10-21, skilled_need_ended), 45 benefit days used net (Sept 20 + 5 less the 09-18 lapse, Oct 21); SNF ABN delivered 10-21 with option 1 for care from 10-24; hospice elected 10-25 (case moved to the hospice room-and-board tier); holds: declined 09-15 (back 09-16), Medicare-stay private hold 09-26 released the same day (back 09-28), Medicare-stay private hold 10-08/09 (back 10-10); application 09-08; September pending accrual 25 days x 398.00 = 9950.00 posted 09-30, settled approved_ma_covered on the 10-02 approval (from 09-01 at 2245.90); September estimate 2245.90 unpaid, past-due notice 10-12; October billed 10-02 and paid (ACH 291.40 on 10-09, standing payee transfer 1954.50 on its due day 10-10); November 2245.90 unpaid, its standing transfer due 11-10; redetermination effective 12-01 -> 2229.70; Medicaid payee funds account with a standing authorization, pension 216.00 monthly, payee benefits 1783.50 (10-03, 11-03) and a 64.20 deposit 11-06, resource-limit notices 10-03 and 11-03, balance 2108.85.
PERSONA: Daniel J. Kessler, rushed before a December assignment; volunteers only the goal; credentials on request; agrees to any correction; runs the ACH payment for the stated amount; no refund or other asks.
STANDARD SOLUTION: find/verify -> case, ledger, Medicare episode + ledger, bed-hold reservations + ledger, funds account + ledger -> 334.96 cost_of_care_cap on October -> 2245.90 trueup_decrease on September -> hand over the 2186.14 ACH advance.
VERIFICATION: scratch ev / t2 / probe scripts (removed at finish) reproduce every figure above; all gates green.
user_scenario: You are Daniel J. Kessler, the son of Lorraine M. Kessler and the agent under her power of attorney. Your mother came to the Keystone Ridge center in Camp Hill straight from the hospital in early September 2026 and lives there now in room 314-B; her Medical Assistance came through this fall and the center receives her Social Security as her payee. You handle the rest of her bills from her checking account. You are calling the business office on a Monday morning, a little rushed, because your company is sending you overseas for all of December and you want her account squared away before you go. What you want is simple: tell me one amount that brings what my mother owes the center for her patient pay fully up to date and also covers her December share ahead of time, and I'll send it right now by bank transfer (ACH) from her account. You do not know what that amount should be and you have not added anything up yourself; you only know you have been paying the remainder the center bills each month after her Social Security is applied. When the agent asks who you are or needs to confirm the account, you give your mother's full name, Lorraine M. Kessler, and, one at a time as they are asked for, her date of birth, 1939-02-14, and the last four digits of her Social Security number, 3826. If asked for contact details on file, your phone is 717-555-0342 and your email is daniel.kessler@kesslerfamily.net; if asked when she was admitted, it was 2026-09-03. You are fine with the business office correcting anything on her account that its rules call for; if the agent tells you something has to be adjusted or posted first, you say to go ahead and do it, without asking for details. You do not want a refund check or anything mailed, and you have nothing else to ask about. You never suggest a figure. Once the agent gives you the amount and hands you the payment to send, you send exactly that amount by ACH on your mother's case, read back the confirmation number you get, thank the agent and end the call. If the agent tells you nothing needs to be paid, you thank them and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 334.96 = max(0, 2245.90 - 1910.94). October: 31 days, daily rate 287.36; no partial-month charge or cost_of_care_cap reduction, case open, the coverage ended on skilled_need_ended; one reservation, no later-ended coverage, the hold (last held day 10-09) ends before the 10-24 span and the 10-25 election, no day away with no bed held -> priced. Standard pricing: no full-coverage or lapsed days; coinsurance days 21. Coinsurance day price: billed to the resident and the Plan L carrier, none as crossover -> nothing. Privately held: the 10-08 Medicare-stay hold -> 10-08 and 10-09, 2 days. Days after coverage: last covered 10-23, advance notice delivered 10-21 with option 1 for care from 10-24 -> 10-24, stopping before the 10-25 hospice election, 1 day. Medicaid days 31 - 21 - 2 - 1 = 7; hospice share from 10-25: 7 days x 287.36 x 95/100 = 1910.94; coinsurance 21 x 0.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.medicaid_case_id: The case id from find_medicaid_cases; one open case.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.charge_entry_id: The 2026-10 actual_notice charge id: 'The review covers the calendar month before the current month and the case's patient pay charge with charge basis actual_notice for that service month' - on 2026-11-09 that is 2026-10, one charge.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.adjustment_reason: cost_of_care_cap: the rule says the reduction 'is posted against that charge with reason cost_of_care_cap'. trueup_decrease reconciles an estimate (this is an actual-notice charge); patient_pay_redetermined needs a notice lowering October (the 2026-11-04 notice takes effect 2026-12-01); not_eligible_month is for months outside eligibility (October is eligible); billing_error is for a wrongly billed amount (2245.90 is the notice amount).

evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Reduce the September 2026 estimate by 2245.90 with reason trueup_decrease.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: medicaid_ext_estimate_month_trueup reconciles the latest month billed as an estimate; the advance is not fixed until that month stands reconciled.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 2245.90 = max(0, 2245.90 - min(2245.90, 0.00)). Estimates billed for 2026-09: 2245.90, no reduction. Notice patient pay: the current notice takes effect 2026-12-01, after 2026-09-01 -> the 2026-10 actual-notice charge, 2245.90. Scope: the September accrual counts 25 days in the center; 1 held day on one reservation; the declined leave 09-15 to 09-16 (1 day); the released hold's day 09-27 (1 day); the skilled admission 2026-09-03 (2 days before); 25 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 30; every Part A day on the 09-03 coverage -> priced. Cost of care: 30 days; full-coverage days 20 less 1 reversed = 19; 1 lapsed-certification day; coinsurance days 5 at nothing (no crossover charge); 1 privately held day; 1 declined day; 1 released day; 2 days before the admission -> Medicaid days 0 -> cost 0.00; actual patient pay 0.00.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.medicaid_case_id: The case id from find_medicaid_cases; one approved case.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.charge_entry_id: The 2026-09 estimated_pending charge: the rule covers 'the latest month billed as an estimate, by service month' - the only estimate.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.adjustment_reason: trueup_decrease: 'the estimate is reduced by the difference with reason trueup_decrease'. cost_of_care_cap is the review of actual-billed or pending-case months; not_eligible_month is for months outside eligibility (September is eligible from 09-01); patient_pay_redetermined and billing_error do not describe a reconciliation.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 2186.14 = max(0, 2229.70 - max(0, 1783.50 + 216.00 - 45.00) + 1910.94). Coming month 2026-12: the current notice (2229.70) takes effect 2026-12-01, on the first day of the coming month. edges.condition: The actual_notice charge of the calendar month before the current month carries a cost_of_care_cap reduction bringing its net amount down to the month's cost of care, wherever that cost is below the charge.
edges.policy_source: The advance is fixed only after the actual charge of the last closed month stands at no more than that month's cost of care.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 2026-10 actual-notice charge stands at 2245.90 with no cost_of_care_cap reduction while October's cost of care is 1910.94.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The 334.96 cost_of_care_cap reduction brings the October charge to 1910.94; with the reconciliation also posted the case balance is 1910.94 owed.

edges.condition: The estimated_pending charge of the latest month billed as an estimate carries a trueup_decrease reduction bringing the estimates billed for that month down to the actual patient pay of the month, wherever that patient pay is below them.
edges.policy_source: The advance is not fixed until the latest month billed as an estimate stands reconciled to the actual patient pay of that month.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The 2026-09 estimate stands at 2245.90 with no trueup_decrease although September's actual patient pay is 0.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisite writes reduce different charges in different service months and neither computation reads the other's: with the reconciliation posted first the cost-of-care reduction is still 334.96, and with the cost-of-care reduction posted first the reconciliation is still 2245.90 (scratch swap runs); both orders leave 1910.94 owed and the advance at 2186.14.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the October reduction the balance carried is 2245.90 owed and the advance is 2521.10 instead of 2186.14.
Without the September reconciliation the balance carried is 4156.84 owed and the advance is 4432.04 instead of 2186.14.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only for one amount that brings the patient pay up to date and covers December, and agrees to adjustments only after the agent says one is needed; it never names October, September, an estimate, a reconciliation, a cost-of-care review, Medicare days, a hold or a reduction.
